newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S.Australia approves Olympic Dam expansion.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S.Australia approves Olympic Dam expansion.

text.p: The South Australian government on Thursday will introduce legislative amendments to facilitate the proposed A$1.25 billion expansion by WMC Ltd of the Olympic Dam mine, with provision for later further expansion.
WMC announced in July it would more than double current annual copper production at the mine to about 200,000 tonnes and raise uranium exide output to 3,700 tonnes from 1,500 tonnes by the year 2001.

Mines Minister Stephen Baker said in a statement the amendments would include provision for expansion up to 350,000 tonnes a year of copper and associated products, subject to meeting all necessary environmental and regulatory requirements.

"Although WMC has no current plans to increase mine output above 200,000 tonnes per annum of copper and associated productions, a comprehensive environmental impact study will be undertaken for a project capable of producing up to 350,000 tonnes per annum copper and associated metals," Baker said.
The original 1982 Olympic Dam and Stuart Shelf indenture was based on annual copper production of up to 150,000 tonnes.

Baker said the State Government and WMC signed an agreement on Thursday to amend the indenture, under which the government will build a A$3.7 million medical facility at the Olympic Dam support town of Roxby Downs in the state's north.

The indenture would also ensure WMC had adequate access to power through the state electricity provider ETSA and provision for a licence to build and operate a pipeline, if required, giving WMC future options for natural gas generated electricity.

Baker said expansion of Olympic Dam was expected to double annual royalty payments to the government from the current A$12 million, a contribution expected to continue for more than 100 years at the proposed rate of production.
